prompt: A student claims: 'For any motion, the total distance travelled is equal to the area under the velocity-time graph.' State the specific condition under which this statement is valid, and explain how total distance must be determined if this condition is not met.
hints: What happens to the sign of the velocity when an object reverses?
How does displacement differ from distance for a return trip?
solution: The statement is valid only when the object moves in one direction throughout (velocity never becomes negative / graph never drops below the time axis). If the object reverses direction (graph goes below the time axis), total distance must be found by summing the absolute values (magnitudes) of the positive and negative areas.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Recall that area below the time axis is negative and subtracts from displacement.
Step 2: Distance is a scalar that cannot decrease.
Step 3: State that the statement holds only when motion is unidirectional.
Step 4: State that when motion reverses, magnitudes of negative areas must be added.

mark_scheme.criterion: States condition: motion in one direction only / velocity is always non-negative / line does not go below the time axis
Explains correction: must add the absolute magnitudes of the areas below the axis to the positive areas
